subsystem: Apocalypse offline mode and library (NOMAD, Kiwix, Kolibri, local model)
summary: Apocalypse is a second, cloud-free Apex (its own dashboard on port 7862, a local qwen3:4b model through a private Ollama on port 11435) plus a resumable downloader for a ~354 GB offline library (Kiwix books, Wikipedia, worldwide map) that is read through Project NOMAD running in Docker Desktop. The code is careful and well tested here (250 tests pass in 12 s), but almost none of it has run end to end on the laptop: the last Start-Apex-Platform.cmd run crashed with the charmap error before Apocalypse came up, Docker/NOMAD was not running, and the local model may never have been prepared. The only part known to be working on the laptop is the library download itself. Two real problems for the owner: new or updated books do not show up in book search until NOMAD rescans its library, and adding about 5 GB or more of extra packs makes 'Download-Apex-Library.cmd 220' silently drop the Wikipedia download that is in progress.

features.name: Start-Apex-Platform.cmd (normal Apex + Apocalypse + cached NOMAD in one console)
features.what: Starts normal Apex in resident mode (run_apex_qwen.py --fast --resident) and the separate Apocalypse dashboard side by side. It also starts NOMAD's Docker containers if they are already built, then opens both pages. If one part fails, the other keeps running. Pressing Restart on the Apocalypse page restarts that part.
features.how_to_use: Double-click Start-Apex-Platform.cmd. Apex opens at http://127.0.0.1:7860/home and Apocalypse at http://127.0.0.1:7862/apocalypse. Options: --offline-only, --no-nomad.

gaps.issue: Books downloaded or updated by Apex's own downloader are invisible to book search until NOMAD rescans its Kiwix library. Download-Apex-Library, Add-Apex-Pack and Update-Apex-Library write ZIM files straight into nomad/storage/zim but never trigger a rescan and never tell the owner to run one. NOMAD rebuilds kiwix-library.xml only when that file is missing or broken, or on a manual rescan. After an update deletes the old ZIM, Kiwix's library still points to the deleted file, so that book disappears from search until a rescan, even though the docs say the old copy keeps working.
gaps.evidence: scripts/setup_apex_apocalypse.py:377 (the only rescan call, in --nomad-readers/--nomad-apps); scripts/prepare_apocalypse_library.py:256-273 (finish_replacements deletes the old file) and 824 (final message mentions readers, not a rescan); NOMAD source admin/app/services/kiwix_library_service.ts ensureLibraryXmlHealthy (rebuilds only when missing or broken); docs/APEX_APOCALYPSE.md:177-180
gaps.fix_hint: After a batch that finished or replaced at least one ZIM, POST http://127.0.0.1:8080/api/zim/rescan-library if NOMAD answers. Otherwise print 'Run Setup-Apex-Apocalypse.cmd --nomad-readers (or Rescan in NOMAD) to make the new books searchable'. Fix the docs sentence too.
gaps.how_confirmed: Grepped the repo: the only rescan call is setup_apex_apocalypse.py:377. Read finish_replacements. Searched the pinned NOMAD source zip with a Python snippet: kiwix-serve runs with --library kiwix-library.xml --monitorLibrary, and the XML is rebuilt only by ensureLibraryXmlHealthy (missing or corrupt file), rescanLibrary, or install/migration.

gaps.issue: Extra packs can silently stop the Wikipedia download. Download-Apex-Library.cmd's size limit counts every archive in the plan, smallest first, and that includes packs added with Add-Apex-Pack. The 220 GB tier has only about 5 GB to spare (the plan without the map is 215.05 GB). Adding 5 GB or more of packs pushes the 127 GB Wikipedia out of the batch. The run then prints 'Done. Every archive up to 220 GB is downloaded' and deletes its after-restart resume entry, while the Wikipedia .part file stays unfinished. The 360 tier has the same problem for the map (6.4 GB spare). Newer versions from Update-Apex-Library can also grow sizes past the margin.
gaps.evidence: scripts/prepare_apocalypse_library.py:607-630 (select_jobs counts every job smallest-first), 787-795 (added packs join plan['jobs']); Download-Apex-Library.cmd:18-21 (90/220/360 tiers), 47-48 (deletes resume entry and says Done)
gaps.fix_hint: Always include archives that already have a .part file or status 'downloading' in the batch. Or leave owner-added packs out of the tier budget. Or print the archives that did not fit before saying Done.
gaps.how_confirmed: Ran select_jobs on the shipped english-worldwide-plan.json: with budget 220, wikipedia_en_all_maxi is selected; after appending a 6 GB 'added' job it is no longer selected (3 GB still fits). Read Download-Apex-Library.cmd lines 47-48.

gaps.issue: If Ollama is not installed, or its private server does not answer within 180 seconds, the whole Apocalypse dashboard fails to start. The code comment says 'The readiness screen remains available', but that only holds when the model weights are missing. ensure_ollama is called outside the try that handles a missing model. Start-Apex-Platform then prints 'Apocalypse: did not start' and port 7862 has no page. The readiness page is still at 7860/apocalypse, but chat there returns 409.
gaps.evidence: scripts/run_apex_apocalypse.py:34 (ensure_ollama before the try at 35-40); scripts/setup_apex_apocalypse.py:53-54 ('Install Ollama' RuntimeError), 82; scripts/run_apex_platform.py:195-198
gaps.fix_hint: Catch RuntimeError from ensure_ollama, print 'Local brain unavailable: ...' and still start the dashboard so the readiness page explains what is missing. Add a test for run_apex_apocalypse.main with no Ollama.
gaps.how_confirmed: Ran ensure_ollama(tmp, 'http://127.0.0.1:11435', offline=True) here with no Ollama installed: it raised RuntimeError 'Install Ollama from https://ollama.com first.' Read run_apex_apocalypse.py:33-40: the call is outside the try/except, so main() exits with code 1.

gaps.issue: Every way of reading books (the page explorer, the AI library tools in both offline and normal Apex, and the reader readiness checks) needs NOMAD running in Docker Desktop. Apex cannot read a ZIM file directly. On the last laptop run Docker Desktop was not running, so no offline book search was possible, even though 127 GB of Wikipedia sits on D:. In a real outage, Docker Desktop and MySQL on the external HDD also have to come up (the docs mention a 9-minute first MySQL start).
gaps.evidence: agent/offline_library.py:106-117 (Library() requires NOMAD's /api/system/services and a running nomad_kiwix_server); scripts/run_apex_platform.py:67-91
gaps.fix_hint: Short term: make Start-Apex-Platform clearly say 'Open Docker Desktop first' and wait for it. Longer term: a fallback that runs kiwix-serve.exe (native Windows build) directly on the ZIM folder when NOMAD is down.
gaps.how_confirmed: Read Library.__init__: the first request is to nomad_readers.BASE (127.0.0.1:8080)/api/system/services. With no answer, call() returns an error JSON and there is no other code path. Grepped for kiwix-serve outside NOMAD: there is none.

gaps.issue: The page check scripts/check_apocalypse_ui.cjs fails. Its fake server does not answer /api/apocalypse/session, which the page now requests, so the badge reads 'SESSION UNREACHABLE' instead of 'NORMAL APEX'. No test runs it, so nobody noticed. The page itself is fine.
gaps.fix_hint: Teach the fake fetch the /session, /library/books and /projects endpoints, and run it from a pytest like test_nomad_readers.py:189 does for the readers check.
gaps.how_confirmed: Ran node scripts/check_apocalypse_ui.cjs: AssertionError, expected /NORMAL APEX/, got 'SESSION UNREACHABLE'. The other two Apocalypse checks pass. Grepped: nothing in tests/ invokes check_apocalypse_ui.cjs.

gaps.issue: The platform launcher looks for docker.exe only in the per-user path %LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\DockerDesktop. The setup script also checks PATH and C:\Program Files\Docker\Docker, which is Docker Desktop's default all-users install. If Docker is installed there, Start-Apex-Platform always prints 'NOMAD: skipped; cached installation or Docker is missing'.
gaps.how_confirmed: Read both functions. The last laptop message ('Docker Desktop was not running') suggests the per-user path exists there, so this is a risk rather than a known failure.

gaps.issue: Start-Apex-Platform.cmd and Start-Apex-All.cmd start normal Apex differently. The platform launcher forces HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 and TRANSFORMERS_OFFLINE=1 on normal Apex, so a Hugging Face model that is not cached yet (speech, voice, embeddings) fails to load there but would download under Start-Apex-All.cmd. Start-Apex-All.cmd never starts Apocalypse or NOMAD.
gaps.fix_hint: Document it in the console banner, or only force the offline flags on the Apocalypse child.
gaps.how_confirmed: Read the lines; this is intentional per the comment at 119-120, but it differs from resident mode started by Start-Apex-All.

gaps.issue: Download-Apex-Apocalypse.cmd is an older overlapping launcher. It downloads the whole 354 GB plan with no size limit, no until-done retry and no resume-after-restart entry, and it refuses to start unless about 374 GB is free. It is easy to confuse with Download-Apex-Library.cmd.
gaps.fix_hint: Delete it, or make it call Setup-Apex-Apocalypse.cmd and then Download-Apex-Library.cmd.
gaps.how_confirmed: Read the .cmd and the free-space check.

gaps.issue: scripts/run_apex_apocalypse.py main() has no direct test. The tests only check that the platform spawns it and that UTF-8 is set. Its Windows Ctrl+Break handler, the port-in-use check and the --resident path are untested.
gaps.fix_hint: Add a test that runs main() with ensure_ollama, verify_model and uvicorn faked.
gaps.how_confirmed: grep -rln run_apex_apocalypse tests/ finds only test_platform_launcher.py and test_text_encoding.py, and neither calls main().

gaps.issue: Two English medical packs (nhs.uk_en_medicines, fas-military-medicine_en) from NOMAD's own lists could not be found in the Kiwix catalog when the plan was made, so they are not being downloaded. They appear only as 'remaining setup'.

needs_from_owner: Run Start-Apex-Platform.cmd again and paste the console output. Check that the 'charmap codec' crash is gone and that the 'Apocalypse: ready' line appears.
Check whether Ollama is installed (where ollama, or %LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\Ollama\ollama.exe). If it is, run Setup-Apex-Apocalypse.cmd once while online to download and test qwen3:4b on D:.

Open Docker Desktop (Linux containers) before Start-Apex-Platform.cmd. If NOMAD has never been built, run Setup-Apex-Apocalypse.cmd --nomad once online (a large download; put Docker's image storage on D: first).
After the Wikipedia download finishes, run Setup-Apex-Apocalypse.cmd --nomad-readers so Kiwix picks up the downloaded books. Then try 'Browse saved books' on the Apocalypse page.
Say which size you gave Download-Apex-Library.cmd (90/220/360). Do not add more than about 4 GB of extra packs before Wikipedia finishes if you chose 220.
Do a real unplugged test: disconnect the internet, open http://127.0.0.1:7862/apocalypse, ask a question and open a book.
Watch GPU memory with Celine's voice and qwen3:4b loaded together (Task Manager > Performance > GPU).
Optional: run Setup-Apex-Courses.cmd once NOMAD is up, and import one small Kolibri channel.

rating.why: Large, careful and well-tested code, and the downloader is proven on the laptop. But the offline brain, NOMAD, the book readers and courses have never run on the PC, book search needs Docker plus a manual rescan, and the launcher's last run crashed.
